key_insight: ApexGO uses generative AI to redesign peptide antibiotics that better kill drug‑resistant bacteria, with candidates validated in vitro and in mouse infection models that match or outperform standard antibiotics.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of rapidly designing effective peptide antibiotics against drug‑resistant bacteria by closing the gap between computational design and experimental validation.
method: Generative sequence design: use of a generative model to propose redesigned peptide variants optimized for antibacterial properties.
In silico multi‑objective scoring to balance potency, stability and safety, followed by synthesis and laboratory screening.
Iterative validation: top candidates tested in bacterial assays and mouse infection models to confirm effectiveness and select leads.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, end‑to‑end use of generative models for therapeutic design, highlighting how AI can accelerate antibiotic discovery when tightly coupled with experimental pipelines. Valuable example for ML practitioners working on design optimization and translational workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: generative model → scoring filters → synthesis → in vitro & in vivo validation
Before/after sequence schematic: original peptide vs ApexGO‑redesigned variant showing key changes
Bar chart comparing antibacterial activity of redesigned peptides vs standard antibiotics (MIC or kill rate)
Mouse infection outcomes: survival curve or schematic showing improved protection by top candidates
paper_title: A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization
paper_authors: Marcelo D. T. Torres, Yimeng Zeng, Fangping Wan, Natalie Maus, Jacob Gardner
